title: Stacked Cards Scroll
summary: Four colourful feature cards pin near the top of the screen one after another, and each card shrinks back and darkens a little as the next one slides over it, leaving a fanned stack of edges.
useWhen: consumer app landing page with three to five features to walk through
onboarding story where each step builds on the last
pricing or plan explainer that should feel like a deck being dealt
friendly fintech or productivity product with a bright palette
techniques: position sticky with per-card top offsets
scroll progress per card from getBoundingClientRect

whyItWorks.how: The stack is built from native position: sticky, each card stuck 18px lower than the one before (--stack-offset). Earlier cards scale from transform-origin 50% 0, so their top edges stay pinned and peek out above the newcomer. You can always see how many cards are behind the current one and where they went.

Per frame the script reads four getBoundingClientRect values, then writes one scale and one --dim opacity per card. Sticky offsets are read once and again on resize, not every frame. Dimming is a pre-filled ::after overlay fading up to 0.4 opacity, not a filter: brightness() repaint.

Scale and dim are linear in scroll position because they are scroll-linked. A card loses 5 percent of its scale (--stack-shrink: 0.05) and gains 0.16 of overlay (--stack-dim) for each later card that arrives, so the first card ends at 0.85 scale under three others. Hover easing is separate: the arrow nudges 5px in 200ms and returns in 160ms.
The cards carry the colour, so the motion stays small. Depth comes from 5 percent steps and a darkening overlay, nothing rotates or bounces, and the copy inside each card never moves.
Under prefers-reduced-motion the cards still stick in turn, since that is plain scrolling, but the scale and dim are forced off with !important, and the call-to-action lift becomes an opacity change.

directions.name: Corporate
directions.change: Use one neutral card colour with a thin border, cut --stack-shrink to 0.03, and replace the illustrations with small product screenshots drawn in SVG.

directions.name: Luxury
directions.change: Go dark, raise --stack-dim to 0.3 so earlier cards fall into shadow, and set headings in a light serif with generous tracking.

directions.name: Experimental
directions.change: Add a slight rotate of about -1.5deg per covered card so the stack fans like a hand of cards, driven by the same arrival value.

pitfalls: Putting each sticky card in its own wrapper ends the sticking as soon as that wrapper scrolls past. All cards must share one parent that spans the whole stack.
Scaling from the centre lets earlier cards shrink away from the top and leaves a gap, so the stack stops reading as a pile.
Animating height or top to fake the stack causes layout every frame. Let sticky do the positioning and transform only the visuals.
Making cards taller than the viewport minus the stack offset hides their bottom edge while pinned.

tunables.name: --stack-offset
tunables.effect: Extra drop per card, which sets how much of each earlier card stays visible.

tunables.name: --stack-shrink
tunables.effect: Scale removed from a card per later card that arrives.

tunables.name: --stack-dim
tunables.effect: Overlay opacity added per later card, capped at 0.4.

reducedMotion: Cards still pin one after another with native sticky positioning, but they do not scale or darken. The call-to-action fades slightly on hover and focus instead of lifting, and the arrow does not move.
